family: DLL side-load into a genuine Google-signed chrome.exe copied to the per-user Chrome install location
evasion_targets: identity.rs Google publisher profile location appdata\local\google\chrome\application\** is user-writable (any user can create it when Chrome is installed system-wide)
engine.rs:5220-5243 on_image_load taints only Unsigned|Invalid; SignatureState::Unknown (first load of a never-seen DLL) never taints
kestrel-win/src/win/translate.rs:987-991 image_load facts = file_or_request(..).unwrap_or_default(): a cache miss (every freshly dropped DLL) is emitted as signed=Unknown and never re-delivered
notes: Red-team round 2. The loader copies the genuine Google-signed chrome.exe into %LOCALAPPDATA%\Google\Chrome\Application\ (pinned per-user Chrome location; absent when Chrome is installed per-machine, creatable by the user) with a malicious chrome_elf.dll. The sensor emits the first image load of a freshly written DLL with signed=Unknown (async enrichment cache miss), and the engine taints only Unsigned/Invalid. chrome.exe is then genuine_browser: owner of every browser store, DPAPI is the browser's own, and the 2.4 MB upload is browser traffic. Same with a DLL signed by a stolen certificate (signed=valid). Added by the fix-round red team (2026-10-25); the engine detects it after the red-team fixes.
